note_tweet.text:
What do ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet actually do all day?

These 6 terms explain how personal agents keep working while you’re offline.

Every big lab has one now: Grok Bot from xAI, Muse from Meta, Dots from OpenAI and, last week, Duet from Anthropic.

Take one example of an agent that reads your inbox overnight and has a brief ready when you open your laptop.

/1 Own computer
The agent gets its own machine in the cloud, with a browser and apps, so it keeps going after you close your laptop. Dots, Grok Bot and Muse each run on one.

/2 Integrations
This is how it reaches your inbox, your calendar and your Slack. Dots connects to 4,000+ apps, and Muse uses integrations to book, shop and pay.

/3 Memory
What it keeps between tasks: who your manager is, which threads you always ignore, what you asked yesterday. Without it, every morning brief starts from zero.

/4 Routines
What starts the work without you asking: a set time, a new email or a Slack mention. Duet's morning brief is a routine.

/5 Approval gates
The moments it has to stop and ask you first. Duet asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything.

/6 Audit log
A record of every action it took, so you can see what happened while you were away. OpenBot, one of the open-source clones, runs every action through a policy check and logs it.

What I haven't seen any launch fully explain yet is:
What happens when a task gets cut off halfway? 
Does it pick up again without sending the same email twice? 
And does your yes on one task carry over to the next? 

Even Anthropic says Duet can still misjudge what's urgent, so I'd test these before connecting an inbox.

Which of these would you want to see before you give an agent your inbox? 👀

note_tweet.text:
This was surprising. 

When I asked the Gemini App to rank the top Artificial Intelligence companies based solely upon Monthly Active Users (MAU) within their entire ecosystem (basically numbers instead of how powerful the AI is), the company currently winning the consumer market surprised me.

Here is the link: https://t.co/Ci98FJFOq9 

Ranking the top ten:

1️⃣ @Apple (via @Siri)

2️⃣ @AlphabetInc (via @GeminiApp, @Google AI search, @YouTube Ask, Workspace)

3️⃣ @Meta (via Meta AI, @Muse, AI assistants on @facebook, @instagram, @WhatsApp & @Threads)

4️⃣ @OpenAI (via @ChatGPT & Dots)

5️⃣ @ByteDance_CN (Doubao & Dola)

6️⃣ @AnthropicAI (via @claudeai & Artifacts)

7️⃣ @Baidu_Inc (via Ernie Bot & Qianfan)

8️⃣ @SpaceX / @spacexai (via @grok & @bot)

9️⃣ @Microsoft (via @MSFTCopilot, @Windows & @github)

🔟 @perplexity_ai 

Of the top ten, only Apple, Alphabet (aka Google), Meta & Open AI have surpassed a billion MAU.

I was surprised by Apple taking the top spot, but in hindsight it makes sense due to the ecosystem. It is the same with Google & Meta too.

Gemini is currently (as of this post) the leading frontier model, with Claude & ChatGPT close behind (based upon @BenchLM_AI & @ArtificialAnlys), although that could change next month (or next week!) due to fierce competition.

I personally use Grok, Gemini & Siri (the latter mostly on my Apple Watch) although many of my friends & family use only ChatGPT.

Claude is the most advanced AI in my personal opinion, as it is heavily used by software developers & the US military (giving it Skynet vibes).

In the end I think Apple, Google & Meta will retain their top positions due to their respective ecosystems, while power users will use Claude, Gemini & ChatGPT.

Sadly I do not see Grok (one of my favorite AI’s) cracking the top three anytime soon due to the ecosystem of @X being much smaller than rival social networks.
